utterances.text: I wasn't beaten because I was in the middle, but the ones who were at the back were beaten, the reservists, not the real soldiers, not the real army.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, the reservists are the army too.

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Not as far as I'm concerned, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And why did they beat people?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: I don't know. They beat the ones who were behind. I was in the middle, so I don't know why they beat those over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Afterwards, you were captured when you tried to escape from the eastern part of Mostar in June; right?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you know that the JNA withdrew from Mostar before the 19th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: As I told you earlier on, I didn't follow all this. I didn't delve into politics. I wasn't interested in politics at all. The real army withdrew. The people that served in the army, they withdrew.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Now let's lighten up. I have a statement here which you gave to the Security Services Centre, the Ministry of the Interior, Bosnia-Herzegovina, in Mostar, on the 23rd of May, 1995. Do you remember giving that statement?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that, but I had a disagreement with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Over what?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Over some photographs, pictures, because each photograph was taken -- they said they had pictures of inmates, of the detainees, and they didn't give me the footage taken with a camera, the pictures taken with a camera, so I had a disagreement with them, I argued with them, and I wanted to ask them whether they had the pictures here. They said they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right, since you had a disagreement with them. Now, that statement is four pages of densely-typed text; do you remember it right?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it in my head.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You signed every page?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In that statement, you nowhere mentioned Seselj's men, there's no mention of a single Seselj's man. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: I think it's in there somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, let's put it on the ELMO and see whether there is any mention of Seselj's men anywhere. We'll look for that. Do you have that? It's 0363-1490. My copy can be put on the ELMO, and we'll look at it together. You should have this, Judges, the statement made by this gentleman to The Hague investigators. It follows on from the statement given to the Muslim police, and you can see that in the third paragraph. And in the fourth, it says the investigator from the Office of the Prosecutor "asked me to say more about the information I had given and clarify some issues discussed in my previous statements." So the OTP is treating these two statements as one, so they should have provided the other one and had it ready. This is not a special -- or, rather, a separate statement given to The Hague investigators, but rather a statement referring to the one given to the Muslim authorities. So I'm only attempting to draw attention to the lackadaisical way this is being done. So let's have a look now at the statement to see whether you mention Seselj's men anywhere. Let's see the entire page, please. So that's the statement. We can see your signature there. Is that your signature? Well, that's the first page of the statement. Can you find the expression "Seselj's men," or "Seselj," or "volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party" mentioned here? Mr. Karisik has this statement, it appears. No?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: I didn't give statements to the military Muslim police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Were the policemen Croats? Who were they?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: I'm not interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You gave it to the official organs of your state. All I want to know is whether there's any mention of Seselj's men here. Let's turn to page 2. You're much faster than we are. Let's look at page 2 and see whether there's any mention of Seselj's men there. Do you have page 2?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: We don't have to read the whole text, because it's almost identical to what you stated orally here, and what you spoke about sounds very convincing. I don't want to cast doubt on your personal experiences. You might have made a mistake due to the state of mind you were in, but that would be immaterial. However, there's no mention of Seselj's men here. Let's look at page 3. So here we are on page 4. Is there any mention of Seselj's men here?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It appears to me there's no mention of that.

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: No, I haven't found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, I didn't expect you to find anything like that. Now, let's -- can I have the document back, please. Now, Mr. Karisik, on the 10th of June, 2004, you spoke with The Hague investigators; is that correct? It says here the 10th of June. You have that statement. I see you have the statement before you. I didn't object to your following along, referring to the statement, although that's not really permitted here, but I didn't object because I thought you were being sincere.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: For the record, the witness did not consult the statement. He flipped through it. I asked him if he was looking at it. He said, "No," and he flipped it back, and he did not refer to it after then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but he had it in front of his eyes. Proceed, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I didn't object, I don't want to enter into a discussion with Madam Biersay on this issue, so as to avoid wasting time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you remember that on the 10th of June, 2004, you gave a statement to The Hague investigators?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You have the statement here?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You see the front page. What ask it say? There's your name there, and it says "10th of June, 2004," at the bottom of the page. So Mr. Karisik, I'm interested in the following: When you started this interview, The Hague investigators had before them the statement you had previous given to the police; is that correct, in 1995?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: They had that statement, and they say here that you gave that statement to the Security Services Centre in Mostar, Ministry of the Interior, on the 23rd of May, 1995. It's in paragraph 3 of your statement to The Hague investigators. And then in paragraph 4: "I have now been asked by the office of the prosecutor investigator who is interviewing me at this time to expand the information provided and to clarify some issues discussed in my previous statement." It's in paragraph 4. You can also see it on the monitor?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes, I can find it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you were able to see that they're only interested in trying to find out something about Seselj or Seselj's men. They were trying to dig something out, suggesting that to you, hoping to get something from you about that. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Well, it was a long time ago. You can dig something up, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, people dig tunnels and mines, so you can dig that up too.

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Well, yes, anything can happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I agree with you, Mr. Karisik. I see that you're a very honest, sincere man, you always speak your mind. So they insisted on that conversation for a long time, and in the end you confirmed something of what they were insisting on; is that right? If Madam Biersay continues doing these gymnastics, she'll get very tired. Now let's go to page 4 and see what it is they dug up. Let's turn to page 4, and let's have it on the ELMO for the public to see, since this is public testimony. So let's have it here. In paragraph 9, you say, and this is what The Hague investigators are actually putting in your mouth: "After that, we started seeing Seseljevci in town. Some Seseljevci wore white hats. Some had todays on and some had sajkacas on, and some had cockades on their hats. They settled in the neighbourhood of Sehovina, East Mostar. The Nevesinje Serbs populated this settlement. Seselj comes from East Herzegovina." Did you see in Mostar, too?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: No, I didn't see you, comrade. I didn't see you, but I heard that Seseljevci and White Eagles and Chetniks were coming. Whose army that was, I just said everyone wanted their own army. Whoever went to war had an army of his own.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, on paragraph 9 it says Seselj comes from East Herzegovina. Someone reading this would feel that you, yourself, saw Mr. Seselj in Mostar. The way it's written, that's what one could infer from this. When the investigator spoke with you, did he ask you whether you had seen Mr. Seselj? Why is this written? Why is there this sentence: "Seselj comes from East Herzegovina"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I gave the statement to someone. I didn't see that, personally. I didn't see him myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It then goes on to say: "Some Seseljevci came from Serbia, and there was some locals who joined them. We noticed that some local Serbs joined the Seseljevci and others supported them. There are a lot of people talking in town that some have gone to join the Seseljevci and some had joined the JNA reserve forces. We also noticed they started wearing cockades and sajkacas. Everybody could recognise them by their appearance." Were these your own words or were they inserted of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: I said that they wore sajkacas and beards and white hats, and I say that. Whose were the White Eagles, whose were the Green Berets, whose were the Chetniks, whose were Seselj's men? They were all together.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you couldn't tell the difference, you couldn't tell them apart?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Well, it didn't say or it wasn't written on their foreheads whether they were JNA or Seselj's men or whatever. If they put on a cockade on their hat, it was a cockade. If it was a moon and star, it was a moon and star. If it was a white hat, it was a white hat.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you hear that Draskovic's men were there?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Well, I'm telling you, I didn't know who was in command of whom.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Very well, sir, but you mention that again somewhere here. In paragraph 14, for example, "we also heard from the JNA soldiers, who were in the firing range, that there were Seseljevci and Red Berets in Mostar." So you always heard it from someone. You couldn't really tell, yourself, who were Seselj's men, who were White Eagles, who were the Serbian Guard?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Well, other people told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. I won't deal with that any longer. I won't weary with that. As you still live in Mostar, are you aware that the District Public Prosecutor's Office in Mostar, as early as in 1993, on the 16th of February, submitted a motion to initiate investigative proceedings against persons who were suspected of having perpetrated a crime against Muslims in Sutina and Borak? Do you know that an investigation was set in motion?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You don't know that. Well, based on that motion, so that we don't have to look at both documents, the District Military Court in Mostar, on the 2nd of March, 1993, issued a decision on conducting an investigative procedure. Can we have that on the ELMO, please, although this is a document given to me by the OTP in some set of documents I was given. If there is any -- there is no ERN number because only the English version had an ERN number. There's a number of the translation here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do we have this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd just like to clarify, Your Honour. This morning, after the break, the Prosecution was presented with two documents with a fax line reading: "June 30th, 2008, 8.54 a.m." There is no ERN numbers, as we do put on our documents typically, and I am unsure of why Mr. Seselj thinks we gave this to him if it arrived at 8.54 this morning -- yesterday, sorry, that would have been yesterday, but we received it nonetheless. Even though the fax line says "June 30th," which would have been yesterday, we received it today after the first break. But irrespective of that, I'm not sure if Mr. Seselj is speaking about the ones he gave us today or some other document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the bottom of the page here, you have the "Reg 9061 Doc/MB." Those are your markings for translation. Why there's no ERN number, how should I know. It was on the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: It is not the markings of our documents, and again I would ask why is a document that has a fax date of June 30, 2008, why does Mr. Seselj believe that this is a document from us? We received this for the first time today in B/C/S, I might add, and I have no idea why he thinks that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, as Ms. Biersay just said, why can you say that this document comes from the OTP? Maybe it does. Maybe your associates found it and faxed it to you, but if they did so, then there would be an ERN number on this document, and it's not there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, let the OTP look for it. It's their document. It wasn't found by my associates. I received this document. Why there's no ERN number, let the OTP explain. Let them look in their archives to see if they have this document or not. Why is there no ERN number? Every time I get material from the OTP, should I check that there's an ERN number? Just imagine that. I received that from the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Biersay, Mr. Seselj is telling us that this document does come from the OTP. Maybe he's right, maybe he's wrong. I don't know. Please check that it is not your document, it does not come from the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. President, Mr. Seselj is the one relying on this document. The burden is on him to show the provenance of this document. This is not our document. All the documents that we provide to Mr. Seselj have an ERN number so that we can track exactly this kind of thing. And as has been pointed out to me, the number at the bottom left of this document is, I believe, a registry number when they receive these documents in B/C/S and they submit it for translation. So, again, I would again tell the Trial Chamber that this is not our document. We did not provide this document to Mr. Seselj, and the burden is on him to prove what the provenance is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the plot thickens, obviously. I don't think we should shed any light on this at the moment. It's quite marginal to know whether it comes from the OTP or from your associates. The important thing is the content of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I can't accept that. Ms. Biersay has just said that this is a registry number, it's not the registry of my expert team for the Defence, it's the registry of the Tribunal. Now, whether I received this several years ago, how should I know and why should I care? It was given to me through the official post of the Tribunal. Now, whether it was sent to me directly through the Registry or the OTP, or whether it arrived from some other trial as an exhibit or piece of evidence, why should I care? If the Prosecutor doubts the authenticity of the document, they can contact the Cantonal Court in Mostar right away and check it out, verify whether it's right or not. I think she's intentionally leading us astray. I did not create the document. We have the registry number here. I didn't submit it for translation. I received it from the competent organs of the Tribunal. And when I say "competent organs," I mean the OTP and Registry. And now you want me to tell me how I received this. How should I know? You've sent me half a million pages of various documents so far, so how should I know? And this is a registry number here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, Mr. Seselj, you received this by fax or how? How did you receive this document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I received this by hand, which is how I receive official documents from the Registry and the Tribunal. I gave them to my legal advisers and assistants to study, and they sent it back -- they faxed it back as a piece of material which would be interesting for the cross-examination of this witness. Now, the Registry can look at the number there and tell us -- let us know where the document is from and what the document is. But as far as I'm concerned, what is important for me is that it's got this official title "The District Court of Mostar," the date and the reference number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right, that's what's important. All the rest is very marginal. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Karisik, it says here -- let's look at this together -- that: "Zjelko Soldo, an Investigating Judge of the Military District Court in Mostar, in the criminal proceedings against Milan Skoro and others accused, accused of committing genocide under Article 141 taken over from the Criminal Code of the former SFRY, with respect to a request for an investigative procedure to be set into motion, tabled by the military prosecutor KT number 37-93 of the 16th of February, 1993, brings in the following decision about conducting an investigative procedure against the following individual." Put that on the overhead projector, please, and as we're dealing with 30 names here, they don't have to be in public. It's enough for Mr. Karisik to take a look at it together with me, so that we can see, Mr. Karisik, that all the 30 individuals on that list, with all their basic data, that they were all inhabitants from Mostar, Vrapcici and Nevesinje, and not a single one of them was from Serbia. That's what it says here. Take a look at the list.

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Well, I'm glad that you raised that issue. You don't have to have 30 people, but I'm happy to see that. I've never seen that, but it has to come out, this kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you know that the Cantonal Court of Mostar tabled a request to the State Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina to unleash criminal proceedings for the killing of Muslims in Sutina and Borak; do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Well, I do know -- I know this court in The Hague. I'm not interested in the court in Bosnia. It can be whatever you like. I'm interested in the Tribunal in The Hague, because in Bosnia they pull this way and that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Look at this list, please.

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Why should I look at it? I have all these names in my head.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You don't want to look at the list?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Well, not really.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You guarantee that there's nobody from Serbia among those 30?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Nobody.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: There are 330, not 30. But Mr. Karisik --

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: You don't have to convince me. We're not here to convince each other of anything. You guarantee that there is nobody there from Serbia among these 30.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well I'm not guaranteeing anything. I'm looking at the list.

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Well I don't want to look at the list. Why should I look at the list. You're guaranteeing that among those 30 names there's nobody from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, do you want to have a look at the list?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: All right, I'll look at the list then.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, I'm happy to see you're in a better frame of mind and want to look at the list now. Let's have it on the overhead projector so Mr. Karisik can see the list. You don't have to mention any of the names, some you have already mentioned, some you have not mentioned. Now, since they haven't been tried yet and the State Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina agreed to try three of these people, whereas all the rest were sent back to the Cantonal Court in Mostar, we're not going to mention any names -- perhaps there's somebody innocent here, not to mention names, but let's go through the list to see where these people come from. Place it on the overhead projector, please. How come I can't see this on my screen. Ah, it's come up now? Right, number 1, can you see that there? His address is Mostar, Zarek 17; right? Just say "yes" or "no?"

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: All right, then I'll say "yes."

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Number 2, the address is Vrapcici 178; right?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes, that's your court over there in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It's your court.

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Well, it's your court. I have a court here, now. I'm just interested in this tribunal. I'm not interested in the court in Mostar. I'm interested in this court here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I agree with you, I'm going to agree with you, but let's move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, please, the problem is not to know which tribunal should deal with this case. We have a document coming from the Mostar tribunal, Mostar court. Mr. Seselj would like you to confirm that the names mentioned are the names of people who live in Mostar or around Mostar. That's all he's asking, and he is asking you to check the addresses of these people. Proceed, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Number 3, can you see that this person's address was Mostar, Potoci, no number?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let's move on to number 4. Was this man's address Mostar, Sutina 19?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: You mean number 4?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes. You know him, don't you?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes, I do know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, there you are, then. Do you know some of the ones before, above?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, you mentioned some of them.

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Well, I mentioned all sorts of people, but it's of no interest.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Just be patient, have a little patience. I know it might be difficult for you to go through this list, but let's try it. Let's look at number 5. Does it say that the address is Mostar, Vrapcici 18? --

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Number 6, does it say that his address was Vrapcici, no number?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Number 7, does it say "Mostar, Vrapcici 127"?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Number 8, does it say "Mostar, Zivote Neimarovica Street, number 17"?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Turn to page 2 now, please. Number 9, does it say that his address is in Vrapcici, and then -- it says "Vrapcici, Mostar," right?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Number 10, does it say the address is Mostar, Prigradjani number 72"?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Number 11, does it say "Vrapcici, Mostar" there for the address?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Number 12, does it say the address is Mostar, Zalik 7/c?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Number 13, does it say that he is from Pluzine, near Nevesinje?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is Nevesinje the neighbouring municipality to Mostar, does it border on Mostar?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Fine. Now, number 14, does it say that the address is Vrapcici 173?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Number 15, does it say that his address is Vrapcici, Mostar?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you mentioned him before, didn't you? Number 16, does it say the address is Cicevo-Konjic, with an address for residency in Mostar, Zeljusa, no number; right?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And Konjic is a neighbouring municipality of Mostar, too?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Number 17, does it say that his address is Mostar, Vrapcici number 44?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Number 18, does it say that the address is Mostar, Vrapcici 13?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: I think the number is 18. It's either 15 or 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It doesn't matter. Vrapcici 13 or 15?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: I think it says "15."

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right, then, Vrapcici 15. I agree with you straight away, you see, sir.

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let's move on. Number 19, does it say that the address is Potoci, Humi-Lisani, Mostar?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That's a village neighbouring on the Mostar municipality?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Number 20, does it say it's Vrapcici 256?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Number 21, does it say that the address is Vrapcici 228?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Number 22, does it say that the address is Vrapcici, Mostar?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let's move on to the third page now, please. Number 23, does it say that the address is Mostar, Vrapcici 140?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Number 24, does it say that the address is Mostar, Vrapcici 32?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: 25, it is this Boro Antelj?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you hear that Boro Antelj was the commander of Draskovic's Serbian Guard in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear about that. That's why I say I don't dwell in politics.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right, so then we're not going to speak about politics, but is this the address of Mostar, Vrapcici no number?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Which number did you say?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Number 26, is this Mostar, Vrapcici 22, the address?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: 27, is the address Mostar, Vrapcici, no number?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: 28, is the address there Kuta Livac, Mostar?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes. What's the name?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Kuta Livac. Kuta Livac, Mostar then.

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So 29, is it Kuta Livac? It says "Livce" here.

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: It's Kuta Livac, Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I don't know Mostar well, but anyway, number 30, is this Mostar, 8 Duk 1 Street?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Did you say 8 Duk 1?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: I can't remember what street it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That's not important, but that's what it says there, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So can you see that the court from Mostar held these as suspects, 30 people, and accused them, and most of them were from Vrapcici, which is a part of Mostar, right, the outskirts of Mostar, right, and all the rest were from Mostar except for one person from Nevesinje and one person from Konjic; right?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: There is this man from Foca, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He used to live in Foca and then moved to Mostar; right?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: No, he was in Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But Foca is in Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes, it is, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right, fine. Now, we have a description of the crime that took place in Sutina and Uborak, and the names of the victims are mentioned here. We don't need to go through that because it's something that actually happened, so I can't deny any crime. If a crime took place, it has to be investigated, and thank you, Mr. Karisik, that will be all of I have no further questions for you. Thank you for having the patience to go through the list with me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I've been through a lot more than the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand you perfectly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Biersay, any redirect?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The first thing I'd like to address, I think it's an error in -- perhaps Mr. Seselj misspoke or perhaps it's a translation error. Page 17, line 21, the witness said he'd stayed one day when being interrogated at the north camp, and in his question posed to the witness at page 44, line 13, I believe, Mr. Seselj is attributed as saying "one month."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's not what I said. It's a translation error. I said "one day," and I identified the fact that Mr. Karisik was arrested by the JNA in April 1992, held for one day, and then he was arrested when the JNA had already withdrawn in June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So then with that, I believe that page 44, that line 13 should be corrected to read "one day," not "one month."

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd like to turn your attention to the local statement that Mr. Seselj showed you. Do you have that statement before you, the one from 23 May 1995?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: 23rd of May, 1995, is that the one you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Yes. And if I could now direct your attention to the beginning of the second paragraph that begins: "Dana, April 9, 1992 ... ," do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: The 3rd of June, 1992? Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: The paragraph that begins: "Dana, April 9, 1992." In that sentence, do you refer to Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: I'm talking about Seseljevci, Chetniks, the White Eagles, the Green Berets. There was all of that, all of that, all complete. Now, who commanded them, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So was that what you clarified with the investigators from the ICTY, you clarified what you meant by "Chetniks" in your 1995 statement?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: All of them together.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. The Prosecutor doesn't have the right to proceed in this way because she's misleading the witness. The whole paragraph must be read. We can see when Mr. Karisik set off for Zalik with the other people there, that they were intercepted by a Land Rover, a police vehicle with four policemen inside, and that among them he recognised one of them, a former MUP worker of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Now, he can repeat, he can keep saying all complete, "Seseljevci," and who knows who else, and a hundred others; but here in the statement he is being very precise. He recognised one man as local being a local and the other four were policemen. That's what it says in the paragraph you just quoted from.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now if you could turn to, I believe, it's page 3, the second paragraph that you see on page 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you have that second paragraph that begins: "Dana, June 13, 1992"?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd like you to count nine lines down from the beginning of that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: On the 30th of June, 1992, at around 2230 hours, on the premises of the locker room, two unknown soldiers entered. Two had helmets and beards. They were wearing olive-green uniforms. One of them was around 35 years old and the other one was around 45.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And could you now read the sentence that begins: "Kada se vozilo"? I apologise for my pronunciation.

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: When the vehicle stopped, one of the Chetniks -- so I said Chetniks because they had beards, that's why I called them Chetniks. One of the Chetniks got out, opened the door and ordered them to step out.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd like to turn your attention to the statement that you gave to the ICTY, so the other statement that Mr. Seselj went through with you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. First of all, this can't be left in the air -- up in the air like that, because where it's most important, the Prosecutor stops, and here's what happened: It says when it first group started to get out, then this one person, one of the soldiers whom the witness referred to as a Chetnik, started shooting and killing, and then Ramo Kolar [phoen] recognised that soldier and said, "Dragan, we've known each other for 30 years," and Dragan killed him straight away.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not "Kolar," it's "Kuko."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Kuko. I read it out wrongly, it's "Kuko." So this is obviously a falsification by the Prosecutor. Obviously somebody recognised the local man who was doing the killing. This Ramo Kuko, who was killed, recognised this person because he had known him for 30 years. So the essential point is something that the Prosecutor is trying to gloss over. And secondly, my second objection is the Prosecutor does not have the right now to ask the witness to look at a statements he gave to The Hague investigators and the Prosecutor. As you cautioned him, Mr. President, last year, and your colleague, Judge Harhoff, what he can do is remind somebody of a date, number, and so on. But the Prosecutor cannot ask the witness to comment on the statement to The Hague investigators. That is something the Prosecutor cannot do. That is something that I can do, but not the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Biersay, I know what you would like to demonstrate, but the problem is we have a text that is in B/C/S, which Mr. Seselj has just read out an excerpt of, when he discussed Mr. Dragan. You didn't mention this, but he seems to be a local. And now you would like to refer to his statement which he gave in 1994 on the same topic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: In 2004, Your Honour, not -- it's not on the same topic. I have covered the points I wanted to, which was in his previous statement in 1995, the witness mentioned "Chetniks," and explained to the Court what he meant by that, meaning Seselj's men, White Eagles, and he puts them altogether in that group; so I am moving on to another issue, which is with respect to paragraph 9 in the statement, which was put forth to the witness by the accused. I would like to ask the witness about this statement that Seselj's come from East Herzegovina. So that's my purpose.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Mr. President, I come back to the previous statement. The Prosecutor failed to explain why she kept quiet about a key fact, glossed over it, and that is that one of the soldiers who did the killing was recognised on the spot. That's the crux of the matter. And, secondly, her interpretation is bad, because we have the witness saying before us that he concluded that there were two Chetniks because they had beards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the same vein, Witness, I thought the accused would have put to you a question on this, but this wasn't mentioned. I would like to get back to the person who stood guard, a person going by the name of Gunjar. I apologise for my pronunciation. You said you had worked with him for 15 years, this Gunjar whom you recognised. Was he a local or was he one of Seselj's men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gunjar, you mean? What party he was, I don't know. What side he was, I don't know, whether he was a Chetnik or in the Seselj's, or White Eagles, or Green Berets. I don't know. I was held captive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But this Gunjar, you worked with him for 15 years, so you knew him, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was a cook.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And he lived next to where you lived, didn't he? He didn't come from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, he was from Nevesinje originally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber if there were locals associated with these Chetniks or Seselj's men, as well as people from other places who were Seselj's men or Chetniks? Were there both locals and people from other places?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Well, I can't say definitely now who was on what side, or party. There was Seselj's side, and then there was the Green Berets' side, and then there was the Vuk Draskovic side. Everybody had his own party or side, and it depended where people decided to go.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: But those people, even though they had different sides, what the Trial Chamber would like to know is: Did they all come from that area, Mostar, or did people come from outside, from other places, to Mostar?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: They came from Montenegro and Serbia, from all sides. People came there from all sides.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Once again, the Prosecutor is intentionally causing confusion. Reservists did come from Serbia, from the Uzice corps, and also from Montenegro; volunteers came in while the JNA was there until the 19th of May, after the 19th of May, nobody came to Mostar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, when you raise this objection and say the Prosecution is causing confusion, do you believe the Trial Chamber can be manipulated in this way, because the Prosecutor is going to put a question to the witness? You may trust the Bench. The Bench can weigh both the question and the answer. There is no confusion in the minds of the Judges. There is a question that's being put, there is an answer that's provided, and the Judges will weigh all of this afterwards. When you say that Ms. Biersay is causing confusion, I will turn around and tell you, no, there is no confusion. The Prosecution holds that it is her duty to do redirect and put additional questions, because you highlighted through your questions a number of issues which clearly are not to the liking of the Prosecutor. This is why the Prosecutor is putting additional questions to the witness, to try and see how things stand, and is trying to put this in line with the Prosecution's standpoint, which may not be the same as that of the Bench. So let the Prosecutor put her questions, and the Bench and the Judges are perfectly capable of drawing their own conclusions. Please proceed, Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now could you turn your attention to paragraph 9 of the statement that you gave to the ICTY. Mr. Seselj asked you some -- he read it, and the Trial Chamber also asked you a question about it. So what I'm interested in, there is a sentence that says Seselj comes from East Herzegovina. I don't know if you know this, but do you know where Mr. Seselj comes from, what area he comes from in general? You were born in Serbia and you spent 30 years in Mostar. Do you know where Mr. Seselj is from, in that sense?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Trebinje.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And where is that, geographically?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Trebinje is in Herzegovina, towards Montenegro, that area.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, I have to object again. The Prosecutor knows full well where I was born, and it states that in the indictment. It says where I was born, and it says that I was born on the 11th of October, 1954, in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Question [as interpreted], with this question Ms. Biersay wanted to highlight the fact that the witness, before the OTP investigators, when he mentioned you, meant to say that you came from Eastern Herzegovina and did not mean to say that you were coming from Eastern Herzegovina to Mostar. That is the meaning of her question. Please proceed, Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't understand anything now, Mr. President. You said the point of her question was that I came from Eastern Herzegovina to Mostar. That's what was interpreted to me. I never visited Mostar during the war. If that is a new case of the OTP, that I came to Mostar from East Herzegovina, I should be told about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Biersay, with her question, wanted to highlight the fact that you are a native of -- that you come from Herzegovina. To be a native of and to come are two totally different things, and to come from. And the witness confirmed this, because he was asked where Mr. Seselj came from, and he said that according to him, he came from Eastern Herzegovina. That's what the witness said, since you are a native of Trebinje. Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd now like to turn your attention to the list, the two pieces -- the two documents that Mr. Seselj gave you. And he went through the 30 names on that list, and specifically, for the record, this is the fax that's dated June 30th, 2008, and the time stamp says "8.56 a.m." One set of documents goes from page 11 to page 14. It has "P-11" to P-14" and the other has "P-7" to "P-10."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. This is a document I received from the OTP, and I mentioned it on the 8th of November of last year in my opening statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'm not sure what the objection is. I'm just making a record of the document we're looking at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not at issue, whether you received the document or not. What we're interested in and why Ms. Biersay is addressing this document again and what it is she wants to demonstrate, and where the documents come from, is really secondary. Please put your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: The 30 names that you read with Mr. Seselj, do you know each and every one of these people?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: I know some quite well.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And of the 30, how many do you think you know, approximately?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Well, I know five really well.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So when you previously described how there are people coming from other places, like Serbia or Montenegro, did any of those people give you their full names?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Well, each of them had a nickname. When people go to work or when they go somewhere, they don't want to be called by their first and last names. They just use their nicknames.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you know that Branislav Vakic was declared vojvoda by Seselj and that he was in the Mostar area from May to June of 1992? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: He knows, himself, that he declared him. If he did something, it will be found out.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you know that? Have you ever heard that name before?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: Not yet. These names were mentioned, but how many of them will be found guilty in the end, that remains to be seen. I'd like to see that, whether they will be people from outside or whether they're local people from Bosnia-Herzegovina, that remains to be seen. Time will tell.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: But my question to you is: Do you know someone by the name of Branislav Vakic, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: REDZEP KARISIK
utterances.text: I don't know him personally. I may have seen him around or on pictures. I didn't have personal contacts with him. I can't recall. It's been 17 years since then.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Witness, on behalf of my colleagues and I personally, also, I'd like to thank you for having come to testify, and I wish you well and a safe journey home. I shall ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, and goodbye.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have some administrative issues to raise, so please don't break early.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I give you the floor, I shall read out an oral decision relating to a particular witness, but I need to find this document. Let's move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, I request that you review your decision for Witness VS-1051, testifying tomorrow under Rule 92 ter, bearing in mind the principles established by yourselves. This is a witness who is the first to testify about the crimes that happened on the Borak Lake and the place called Zijemlje.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that we move to private session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, I'm not mentioning any names, so we cannot move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, nonetheless we shall move into private session, because VS-051 [as interpreted] has been granted protective measures. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Tomorrow, then, in open session, we will start with the witness. We will very quickly move back into private session because protective measures were granted. Ms. Biersay, one last thing?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In the morning, it is my intention to address the protective measures for 1052. And given the time, would the Trial Chamber prefer that I do that in the morning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We will deal with this tomorrow morning. So the hearing is adjourned, and we will meet tomorrow at 8.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 2nd day of July, 2008, at 8.30 a.m. 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.14 p.m.,
